items.title: War ka soo yeeray Israa’iil oo horseedi kara dagaal Turkey
items.description: Tel Aviv (Caasimada Online) – Xildhibaan ka tirsan baarlamaanka Israel ayaa Turkey ku tilmaamay “cadowga qaranka”, xilli ay cirka isku sii shareereyso xiisadda u dhexeysa Ankara iyo Tel Aviv, oo horey ugu kala fogaa dagaalka Gaza, weerarrada Israel ee Lubnaan iyo Suuriya, iyo loollanka saameynta gobolka. Ariel Kellner, oo ka tirsan xisbiga Likud ee uu hoggaamiyo ra’iisul wasaare Benjamin Netanyahu, ayaa wareysi uu siiyay idaacadda Galei Israel ku sheegay in Turkey ay tahay “dal cadow ah si kasta oo loo eego.” Kellner ayaa sidoo kale weerar afka ah ku qaaday madaxweynaha Turkey Recep Tayyip Erdogan, isaga oo ku tilmaamay “kaligii taliye doonaya inuu soo celiyo khilaafadii Islaamka.” “Waa qof aad khatar u ah oo Israel si qoto dheer u neceb,” ayuu yiri Kellner, isaga oo intaas ku daray in Israel iyo dalalka reer Galbeedka ay tahay inay Erdogan u arkaan “khatar”. Hadalka Kellner ayaa yimid kadib markii Erdogan uu sheegay in weerarrada Israel ee Suuriya iyo Lubnaan ay gaareen heer ay khatar ku yihiin amniga Turkey, isla markaana waxa uu ugu yeeray “gardarrada Israel” ay halis ku tahay amniga gobolka iyo kan caalamka. “Israel waa in la joojiyaa, tani waa waajib saaran bani’aadannimada,” ayuu yiri Erdogan. Netanyahu ayaa si kulul uga jawaabay hadalkaas, isaga oo Erdogan ku tilmaamay “kaligii taliye Yuhuud naceyb qaba.” Hase yeeshee, madaxweynaha Mareykanka Donald Trump, oo wax laga weydiiyay hadalka Erdogan, ayaa sheegay inuu yahay “saaxiib wanaagsan” oo ay si wanaagsan u wada shaqeeyeen. “Waa saaxiib aad u wanaagsan oo aan leeyahay, si fiicanna waan u wada shaqeynay. Aad ayaan u jeclahay,” ayuu yiri Trump. Turkey ayaa noqotay mid ka mid ah dalalka ugu codka dheer ee dhaliila Israel, gaar ahaan dagaalka Gaza, weerarrada Iran, Lubnaan iyo tallaabooyinka ay Israel ka waddo Suuriya. Ankara ayaa Israel ku eedeysay inay hurineyso colaado gobolka ka jira, isla markaana ay caqabad ku tahay nabadda Bariga Dhexe. Xiriirka Turkey iyo Israel ayaa si weyn hoos ugu dhacay bishii May 2024, markii Ankara ay ku dhawaaqday inay joojisay ganacsigii ay la lahayd Israel. Turkey ayaa sidoo kale ku biirtay dacwadda Koonfur Afrika ay ka gudbisay Israel ee taalla Maxkamadda Caalamiga ah ee Caddaaladda, taas oo la xiriirta dagaalka Gaza. Si kastaba, inkastoo xiriirka ganacsi ee tooska ah la jaray, warbixinno ayaa sheegaya in badeecooyin Turkish ah ay weli Israel ku gaaraan dalal saddexaad, halka saliidda Azerbaijan ee marta dhuumaha Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan ay weli gaarto Israel iyadoo ka soo baxda dekedo Turkish ah. Xiisadda labada dal ayaa todobaadyadii u dambeeyay yeelatay wajiyo cusub, kadib markii saraakiil Israel ka tirsan ay si furan u bilaabeen inay Turkey ku tilmaamaan cadow mustaqbalka halis gelin kara Israel. Dabayaaqadii bishii May, wasiirka dhaqanka iyo ciyaaraha Israel, Miki Zohar, ayaa isna sheegay in Turkey loo baahan yahay in loola dhaqmo sidii “dal cadow ah”, isaga oo ka digay in Ankara ay noqon karto mid ka mid ah khataraha ugu waaweyn ee Israel wajahdo. “Waa inaan bilownaa inaan Turkey ula dhaqanno sidii dal cadow ah,” ayuu yiri Zohar. Wasiirka ayaa intaas ku daray: “Haddii Turkey ay doorato waddada dagaalka ee naga dhanka ah, shaki kuma jiro inay bixin doonto qiimo aad u culus. Israel way taqaan sida ay isu difaacdo iyo sida ay u dhaawacdo kuwa waxyeelleeya.” Hadalladan kulul ayaa muujinaya in xiriirka Turkey iyo Israel uu galay marxalad aad uga fog khilaaf diblomaasiyadeed oo caadi ah. Labada dhinac ayaa hadda si furan isugu adeegsanaya erayo dagaal iyo hanjabaad, xilli dagaalka Gaza iyo loollanka saameynta Suuriya ay sii kala fogeynayaan Ankara iyo Tel Aviv. Turkey, oo xubin ka ah NATO, ayaa muddooyinkii dambe isku dayeysay inay kordhiso saameynteeda Suuriya kadib isbeddelladii siyaasadeed ee dalkaas ka dhacay, halka Israel ay sii waddo weerarro ay sheegto inay ku beegsaneyso khataro amni oo ka iman kara Suuriya iyo Lubnaan. Falanqeeyayaasha gobolka ayaa sheegaya in khilaafka labada dal uu ka tarjumayo isbeddel ballaaran oo ka socda Bariga Dhexe, halkaas oo dagaalka Gaza uu dib u qaabeeyay xiriirrada siyaasadeed, isla markaana uu sare u qaaday tartanka awoodda ee u dhexeeya Turkey, Israel iyo dalalka kale ee gobolka. Inkasta oo aanay weli muuqan calaamado muujinaya in khilaafka labada dal uu isu beddelayo iska horimaad militari oo toos ah, haddana hadallada ka soo yeeraya madaxda iyo siyaasiyiinta labada dhinac ayaa muujinaya in xiriirka Ankara iyo Tel Aviv uu gaaray heerkii ugu xumaa sanadihii u dambeeyay. items.title: Itoobiya oo shaacisay in TPLF ay duulaan tahay iyo dagaalka oo maalmaha soo socda…
items.description: Addis Ababa (Caasimada Online) — Dowladda Itoobiya ayaa Khamiistii sheegtay in xoogag ku sugan gobolka waqooyiga dalka ee Tigray ay diyaarinayaan weerar ka dhan ah dowladda federaalka, tallaabo dhalisay cabsi cusub oo laga qabo in dalkaas uu dib ugu laabto dagaalkii dhiigga badan ku daatay ee dhowaan la soo afjaray. Ciidamada Tigray ayaa dagaal laba sano socday la galay ciidamada federaalka Itoobiya, kuwaas oo ay garab siinayeen maleeshiyaad maxalli ah iyo ciidamo ka socday Eritrea. Dagaalkaas, oo socday intii u dhaxeysay 2020 iyo 2022, ayaa lagu dilay ku dhowaad 600,000 oo qof, sida ay muujinayaan qiyaaso loo aaneynayo Midowga Afrika. Dagaalka ayaa ku dhammaaday heshiis nabadeed oo lagu gaaray Pretoria sanadkii 2022, balse heshiiskaas ayaa bilihii u dambeeyay la kulmay cadaadis sii xoogeysanayay, iyadoo dhinacyadu marar badan isku eedeeyeen jebinta qodobbadii lagu heshiiyay. Xiisadda ayaa sii korortay kadib markii dagaallo toos ah ay mar kale dhexmareen ciidamada Tigray iyo ciidamada federaalka dabayaaqadii 2025, markii ugu horreysay tan iyo markii la saxiixay heshiiska nabadda. Digniin ka timid Addis Ababa Wasiirka arrimaha Bariga Afrika ee Itoobiya, Getachew Reda, iyo madaxa sirdoonka dalkaas, Redwan Hussein, ayaa sheegay in garab mayal-adag oo ka tirsan Jabhadda Xoreynta Shacabka Tigray ee TPLF uu go’aansaday inuu “maalmaha soo socda” weerar ku qaado dowladda federaalka. Labada mas’uul ayaa qoraal ay ku daabaceen Al Jazeera ku sheegay in TPLF ay isku diyaarineyso inay “huriso dagaal cusub”, iyagoo ku eedeeyay inay taageero ka heleyso Eritrea, oo xiriirkeedu dowladda Addis Ababa uu aad u xumaaday. TPLF weli si degdeg ah ugama jawaabin eedeymaha cusub. Dowladda federaalka ayaa horay u sheegtay in TPLF ay xiriir dhow la yeelatay Eritrea, inkastoo kooxdaas ay eedeymahaas beenisay. “Waa lama huraan in cid kasta oo saameyn ama awood ku leh TPLF iyo taageerayaasheeda Asmara ay cadaadiskii ugu xoogga badnaa saarto, si looga hortago in dalka uu dib ugu laabto dagaal,” ayay ku yiraahdeen qoraalka. Waxay sidoo kale ka digeen in dib u bilaabashada dagaalka ay noqon doonto mid halis ah, islamarkaana “cawaaqib culus ku yeelan doonta gobolka”. Getachew Reda iyo Redwan Hussein ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in kulamo u dhexeeya saraakiil Eritrean ah iyo xubno ka tirsan TPLF ay ka dhacayaan caasimadda Eritrea ee Asmara, magaalada Mekelle ee xarunta Tigray, iyo gudaha Sudan. Eedeymahan ayaa imaanaya xilli Geeska Afrika uu wajahayo xiisado is-biirsaday. Bishii May, Itoobiya iyo Sudan — oo lafteedu dagaal sokeeye ku jirtay tan iyo 2023 — ayaa is dhaafsaday eedeymo ku saabsan in mid walba uu ku xadgudbay dhulka kan kale, islamarkaana uu taageero siiyay xoogag mucaarad ah. Xiriirka Itoobiya iyo Eritrea ayaa sidoo kale sii xumaaday sanadihii u dambeeyay, gaar ahaan kadib heshiiskii Pretoria oo Eritrea aysan qeyb ka ahayn. Asmara ayaa horay u diidday eedeymaha Addis Ababa ee la xiriira faragelinta gudaha Itoobiya, halka dowladda Abiy Ahmed ay ku adkeysatay in Eritrea ay taageereyso kooxo hubeysan. Heshiis nabadeed oo sii daciifaya TPLF ayaa muddo ku dhowaad 30 sano ah awood weyn ku lahayd siyaasadda Itoobiya, kahor inta uusan Ra’iisul Wasaare Abiy Ahmed xukunka imaan sanadkii 2018. Xukuumadda Abiy ayaa sanadkii hore TPLF ka mamnuucday dhaqdhaqaaq siyaasadeed, balse kooxda ayaa weli awood ballaaran ku leh gudaha Tigray, halkaas oo ay ku heysato ciidan u gaar ah. Dabayaaqadii April, TPLF ayaa sheegtay inay dib u soo celisay baarlamaankii gobolka, kaas oo dowladda federaalka ay ku tilmaantay sharci-darro. “Si cad oo ka dhan ah heshiiskii 2022, haraadiga TPLF waxay burburiyeen maamulkii ku-meel-gaarka ahaa ee gobolka, waxayna dhisteen maamul sharci-darro ah oo iyaga u gaar ah,” ayay ku yiraahdeen labada mas’uul qoraalkooda. Tallaabadaas ayaa sare u qaaday walaaca laga qabo in gobolka Tigray uu yeesho laba maamul oo is diidan, taas oo sii adkeyn karta fulinta heshiiskii Pretoria iyo dadaallada dib-u-heshiisiinta. Tigray ayaa lahaa dad gaaraya ku dhowaad lix milyan kahor dagaalkii 2020-2022. Ku dhowaad hal milyan oo qof ayaa weli ku barakacsan saameynta dagaalka, iyadoo gobolka uu sidoo kale wajahayo dhaqaale xumo weyn kadib markii la jaray kabkii dhaqaale ee federaalka. Gobolka Tigray kama qeybgelin doorashadii guud ee Itoobiya ee qabsoontay 1-dii June, taas oo xisbiga Ra’iisul Wasaare Abiy Ahmed ee Prosperity Party si weyn loogu saadaalinayo inuu ku guuleysto. Xiisadda cusub ayaa kusoo aadeysa xilli dowladda Itoobiya ay weli wajahayo colaado kale oo gudaha ah, gaar ahaan gobollada Amhara iyo Oromia, taas oo ka dhigeysa xaaladda dalka mid aad u nugul. Haddii dagaal cusub uu ka qarxo Tigray, waxaa laga cabsi qabaa inuusan ku ekaan waqooyiga Itoobiya oo keliya, balse uu saameyn ku yeesho guud ahaan Geeska Afrika, oo horeyba ula daalaa dhacayay dagaallo, barakac iyo loollan siyaasadeed oo heer gobol ah. items.title: The missing layer: Somalia’s governance  crisis
items.description: By Wilo Abdulle Somalia does not lack laws. It does not lack institutions, frameworks, or internationally drafted roadmaps. What it lacks, persistently and at great cost, is the quality of leadership required to honestly breathe life into those structures. This is the conversation Somali political and intellectual discourse keeps circling without landing on. It is time to land on it. There is a Somali saying that frames this moment with precision: “Ammuuri waqtigeeday falantaa.” All matters, time is their executor. Somali oral tradition This is not a counsel of patience. It is a recognition that time itself is the active agent, the one with the real power to act on human affairs regardless of what people in positions of authority choose to do or avoid doing. Unresolved matters do not dissolve themselves or disappear. They accumulate. The governance failures that Somali citizens have lived with across three decades are not abstract historical events. They are active, compounding, and daily in their consequences. When we speak of governance failure in Somalia, we tend to reach for external explanations first. Foreign interference, historical trauma, colonial division, regional fragmentation, donor conditionality. These forces are real and they matter. But they have also become a convenient curtain behind which a more uncomfortable truth hides: that the people occupying the highest seats of Somali governance have frequently lacked the professional formation, the strategic depth, and the ideological grounding necessary to govern a complex, wounded, and proud society toward stability. Leadership is not a title. It is a practice that must be built. It requires stewardship, the tested ability to hold something in trust for others. It requires strategic wisdom and vision, not just cleverness in negotiation or survival in political games, but the capacity to read a society’s historical trajectory and make decisions that compound in the right direction over time. It requires qualifications that are not merely academic but experiential, ethical, and contextually intelligent. Somalia needs leaders who understand not just policy but people, not just power but accountability. Without these dimensions embedded in governance, what Somali citizens witness is not a state in progress but a state that keeps failing at the same joints, in the same ways, for the same reasons in every four years. A captured field A population cannot elect or select its way to competent governance if the options available to it are uniformly shaped by the same internal war criminals connected to external colonial networks, the same foreign-cultivated or trained, foreign-funded, internally invalidated and externally validated political elites whose first loyalties are too often to the institutions that locally fabricated and financed their training rather than to the communities that raised them. This is not an argument against education, lived experience, or international engagement. It is a valid argument for rootedness. Let us be precise about what is happening in Somalia’s political field, because imprecision has protected the wrong people for too long. The first distortion is the most dangerous. A significant portion of the individuals who have occupied or continue to seek Somalia’s highest offices carry direct or indirect responsibility for the violence of the 1990s and the years that followed. These are not historical abstractions. They are men whose decisions contributed to the destruction of Somali state institutions, whose militias displaced millions, whose negotiations in Nairobi and Djibouti and Addis Ababa were conducted not in the interest of reconciliation but in the interest of their own re-entry into power. The international community, for reasons of its own convenience, recycled these figures into the transitional frameworks because they controlled territory and commanded armed men. Legitimacy was manufactured. Community consent was bypassed. And so the Somali state, in its post-collapse reconstruction, was handed back in significant part to the architects of its collapse. That transaction has never been fully named, and it has never been resolved. Its consequences are still governing. The second distortion operates alongside the first, and in many cases merges with it. Somalia’s political elite has been substantially shaped by an external validation economy that has almost nothing to do with Somali civic trust. The pathway to leadership has too often run through foreign capitals, international NGO headquarters, UN agency rosters, and diaspora networks whose relationship to the Somali interior is mediated by remittances and nostalgia rather than daily accountability. The individuals produced by this pathway arrive fluent in the language of international frameworks, capable of writing the right reports, saying the right things in the right rooms in Geneva or Brussels or Washington. They are legible to external audiences. They are frequently illegible to the communities they are supposed to serve. This illegibility is not accidental. It is structural. When a political figure’s career is built on external recognition rather than internal mandate, their accountability runs upward and outward, toward the funding body, the diplomatic mission, the international monitor, not downward and inward toward the constituents whose lives their decisions shape. The community that raised them is not the audience that matters for their survival. This is what internal invalidation means in practice. It means that ordinary Somali citizens, the farmer in Shabele or Juba, the displaced woman in Baidoa, the young man in Kismayo with no formal employment, hold no real leverage over the people governing them, because those governors/presidents do not require their validation to stay in power. External legitimacy substitutes for domestic legitimacy. And the gap between the two is where governance goes to die. The third distortion is the fabrication of local credentials. Somalia has developed an elite of male dominated of political actors who present domestic roots and community ties as their qualification while operating almost entirely within externally financed structures. The local NGO funded by a single foreign government and answerable to its reporting requirements. The civil society platform convened not from grassroots demand but from a project design document written in a donor country. The policy institution whose research agenda is determined by what the funder country’s interests and wants to know rather than what the community needs answered. These structures are not neutral. They produce a form of local knowledge curated for external consumption, a version of Somalia that is dehumanized, manageable, legible, and fundable, rather than a version of Somalia that is real, human-centered, contradictory, and sovereign. The people trained and promoted within these structures carry that curated version as their political worldview. In most cases they have genuinely internalized it. That is what makes the problem so persistent and so difficult to dislodge. The democratic aspiration and its distorted field The democratic aspiration at the heart of Somalia’s constitutional order is one person, one vote. But the vote only has meaning if the field of candidates represents genuine alternatives rooted in Somali social, economic, and political realities. When that field has been pre-selected, narrowed by war-era bargains, external patronage networks, and the systematic exclusion of genuinely community-accountable voices, then the act of voting becomes a performance rather than a decision. Somali citizens are being asked to choose between options that were never really theirs to begin with. Somali political culture has too often rewarded group loyalty over competence, clan arithmetic over institutional qualification, and short-term coalition management over long-term state building. The result is administrations that are politically balanced on the surface but strategically hollow at the core. Ministries staffed by appointment rather than merit. Decisions made by calculation rather than by policy. A governance elite whose survival does not depend on getting things right for the people but on managing relationships with those who finance and legitimize them from outside. This is not a peripheral problem. It is the central problem. Somalia has been governed for too long by a political men dominated elite that is simultaneously too foreign in its accountability and too compromised in its history. These two conditions reinforce each other. The warlord  war profiter who reinvented himself as a senator, parliamentarian or statesman needed international cover to do so. The international community needed local partners willing to sign agreements and staff ministries. A transaction was made. The Somali people were not party to it. That transaction is still running, and it runs through every election cycle, every new administration, every freshly drafted national development plan that goes unread by government officials and thereafter unimplemented because it was never rooted in the society it claimed to serve. What rootedness actually means Somali tradition understood the architecture of accountability before any modern governance framework was drafted. There is a question that was asked and answered collectively for generations: “Yaa dhibaato tirsanaya? Geedka hoostiisa ayaa xeerbeegtu ku kulmi jireen, kagana xaajoon jireen, kuna xalin jireen dhib walba. Sidaana bulshadu uga qaybqaadan jirtey qeexida, soo bandhigida, falanqaynta iyo xalinta xaalad walba oo bulshada dhexdeeda ka jirta ama banaankeeda kasoo wajahda.” Who has a problem? Who has an issue? Under the tree, the elders of customary law (local council members) would gather, consult, and resolve every hardship. That is how the community participated in defining, presenting, analyzing, managing, and resolving every situation arising from within the community or approaching it from without. Somali oral tradition The question “yaa dhibaato tirsanaya”, who has a problem, who has an issue, was an open call. Any member of the community could bring their matter to the tree. Access was universal. That is the first thing to understand. The second thing, equally important and far less discussed, is that the seat at the tree was not open to anyone. The Xeerbeeg were not elected by whoever showed up, nor appointed through political deals, nor selected to satisfy a quota. Membership was earned through a standard of demonstrated qualification that many of Somalia’s current parliamentarians could not meet. To sit as xeerbeeg, a person had to carry knowledge across multiple domains simultaneously: mastery of customary law and its application, grounding in religious principles and their moral demands, and familiarity with broader universal norms and the logic of agreements between peoples. Beyond knowledge, they had to demonstrate active listening, the capacity to hear what was being said beneath what was being said. They had to bring skilled negotiation, holding competing interests without collapsing them prematurely into a false resolution. They had to exercise critical analysis, reading situations in their full context rather than their surface presentation. And above all, they had to have a proven record of judgment grounded in justice and accountability, not in loyalty, not in personal advantage, not in the preferences of whoever held the most power within and without the communities they represent. This is the contrast that must be named plainly. Somalia’s federal parliament today is filled through a process shaped by clan arithmetic, financial transactions, and political patronage. The tree was filled through a process shaped by proven wisdom, plural knowledge, and demonstrated integrity. The parliament claims to be the more modern institution. In the matter of qualification standards for those who hold power over others, it is the more degraded one. None of the argument in this piece is against education, international engagement, or community and diaspora participation. Somalia cannot and should not close itself off from the world. Somali diaspora communities carry extraordinary intellectual, financial, and civic resources, and their engagement with the country’s development is not only legitimate but necessary-lifeline. International partnerships, when structured honestly,without back-thought interests, can support rather than distort. The argument is for the condition that makes all of these things useful rather than extractive, and that condition is rootedness. Rootedness in this context means political legitimacy that originates from within Somali society, not from without. It means leaders whose formation, however international their education, has been tested against the lived realities of Somali communities, whose judgment has been shaped by proximity to ordinary suffering rather than distance from it. It means accountability structures that run toward the people rather than away from them. It means the vetting of candidates and officials against standards of integrity that include their conduct during the years of violence, their record of resource, stewardship, and their demonstrated commitment to the communities they claim to represent. It means that the question of who leads Somalia is answered by Somali people operating from an informed position, not choreographed into endorsing a field pre-selected by external interests and internal power brokers before any vote is cast. Locally grounded durable solutions are not a slogan. They are a method. They require that the people designing and implementing governance carry real accountability to the communities affected, not just to the donor program cycle. The leader who can be questioned under the tree, figuratively or literally, who must return to the community and answer for what was done in its name, is a fundamentally different figure from the leader whose political survival is managed in a hotel conference room in another country or in an office of another country’s ministry of foreign affairs. The cost and the call The cost of the missing layer is not abstract. It shows up in a child who cannot access a functioning clinic. In a farmer whose land dispute goes unresolved for decades. In a woman whose testimony carries no weight in any formal institution. In a young person who sees clearly that the system was not built for them and was never intended to answer to them. These are not governance statistics. They are the accumulated cost of transactions conducted over the heads of ordinary Somali people, in their names, without their consent. Somalia has enormous intellectual capacity, an extraordinary diaspora, communities that have maintained social cohesion through decades of state collapse, and a younger generation that is watching and forming judgements about what is possible. What that generation needs to see is that the question of who leads and on what basis is being taken seriously, not managed, not performed for international audiences, but genuinely reckoned with as the foundational question of the country’s future. Identifying the missing layer clearly is the first act of rebuilding it. That layer is not a technical fix, not a new framework, not another round of international consultations. It is a political culture that demands rootedness as the price and base of power, that insists on accountability as a condition of legitimacy, and that refuses to extend either to figures whose record disqualifies them regardless of how effectively they have been rebranded. It is a civic infrastructure capable of making that demand stick. The state exists to serve its people. Somalia deserves leadership that answers to Somalia. Not to Mogadishu’s political season, not to the preferences of a capital on another continent, but to the lived realities of Somali people across every region of this country. That kind of leadership does not arrive by accident. It is cultivated, demanded, and chosen/elected. The question of who has a problem, who has an issue, was once answered under a tree, by people whose accountability ran in one direction only: toward the community. Rebuilding that direction is not a return to the past. It is the precondition for any viable future. Ammuuri waqtigeeday falantaa. All matters, time is their executor. The demand for rooted, accountable leadership in Somalia is not idealism. It is the most practical political position available to a people who have waited long enough. Wilo Abdulle, Email : Wilo.abdulle@gmail.com —— Wilo is Somali writer and governance practitioner working at the intersection of policy, equality, inclusion, human rights, community accountability, and the politics of development in the Horn of Africa. Her work on governance, accountability, and development in Somalia is rooted in a single conviction: that Somalia’s solutions must be Somalia’s own. When a political figure’s career is built on external recognition rather than internal mandate, their accountability runs upward and outward, toward the funding body, the diplomatic mission, the international monitor, not downward and inward toward the constituents whose lives their decisions shape. The community that raised them is not the audience that matters for their survival. This is what internal invalidation means in practice. It means that ordinary Somali citizens, the farmer in Shabele or Juba, the displaced woman in Baidoa, the young man in Kismayo with no formal employment, hold no real leverage over the people governing them, because those governors/presidents do not require their validation to stay in power. External legitimacy substitutes for domestic legitimacy. And the gap between the two is where governance goes to die. The third distortion is the fabrication of local credentials. Somalia has developed an elite of male dominated of political actors who present domestic roots and community ties as their qualification while operating almost entirely within externally financed structures. The local NGO funded by a single foreign government and answerable to its reporting requirements. The civil society platform convened not from grassroots demand but from a project design document written in a donor country. The policy institution whose research agenda is determined by what the funder country’s interests and wants to know rather than what the community needs answered. These structures are not neutral. They produce a form of local knowledge curated for external consumption, a version of Somalia that is dehumanized, manageable, legible, and fundable, rather than a version of Somalia that is real, human-centered, contradictory, and sovereign. The people trained and promoted within these structures carry that curated version as their political worldview. In most cases they have genuinely internalized it. That is what makes the problem so persistent and so difficult to dislodge. The democratic aspiration and its distorted field The democratic aspiration at the heart of Somalia’s constitutional order is one person, one vote. But the vote only has meaning if the field of candidates represents genuine alternatives rooted in Somali social, economic, and political realities. When that field has been pre-selected, narrowed by war-era bargains, external patronage networks, and the systematic exclusion of genuinely community-accountable voices, then the act of voting becomes a performance rather than a decision. Somali citizens are being asked to choose between options that were never really theirs to begin with. Somali political culture has too often rewarded group loyalty over competence, clan arithmetic over institutional qualification, and short-term coalition management over long-term state building. The result is administrations that are politically balanced on the surface but strategically hollow at the core. Ministries staffed by appointment rather than merit. Decisions made by calculation rather than by policy. A governance elite whose survival does not depend on getting things right for the people but on managing relationships with those who finance and legitimize them from outside. This is not a peripheral problem. It is the central problem. Somalia has been governed for too long by a political men dominated elite that is simultaneously too foreign in its accountability and too compromised in its history. These two conditions reinforce each other. The warlord  war profiter who reinvented himself as a senator, parliamentarian or statesman needed international cover to do so. The international community needed local partners willing to sign agreements and staff ministries. A transaction was made. The Somali people were not party to it. That transaction is still running, and it runs through every election cycle, every new administration, every freshly drafted national development plan that goes unread by government officials and thereafter unimplemented because it was never rooted in the society it claimed to serve. What rootedness actually means Somali tradition understood the architecture of accountability before any modern governance framework was drafted. There is a question that was asked and answered collectively for generations: “Yaa dhibaato tirsanaya? Geedka hoostiisa ayaa xeerbeegtu ku kulmi jireen, kagana xaajoon jireen, kuna xalin jireen dhib walba. Sidaana bulshadu uga qaybqaadan jirtey qeexida, soo bandhigida, falanqaynta iyo xalinta xaalad walba oo bulshada dhexdeeda ka jirta ama banaankeeda kasoo wajahda.” Who has a problem? Who has an issue? Under the tree, the elders of customary law (local council members) would gather, consult, and resolve every hardship. That is how the community participated in defining, presenting, analyzing, managing, and resolving every situation arising from within the community or approaching it from without. Somali oral tradition The question “yaa dhibaato tirsanaya”, who has a problem, who has an issue, was an open call. Any member of the community could bring their matter to the tree. Access was universal. That is the first thing to understand. The second thing, equally important and far less discussed, is that the seat at the tree was not open to anyone. The Xeerbeeg were not elected by whoever showed up, nor appointed through political deals, nor selected to satisfy a quota. Membership was earned through a standard of demonstrated qualification that many of Somalia’s current parliamentarians could not meet. To sit as xeerbeeg, a person had to carry knowledge across multiple domains simultaneously: mastery of customary law and its application, grounding in religious principles and their moral demands, and familiarity with broader universal norms and the logic of agreements between peoples. Beyond knowledge, they had to demonstrate active listening, the capacity to hear what was being said beneath what was being said. They had to bring skilled negotiation, holding competing interests without collapsing them prematurely into a false resolution. They had to exercise critical analysis, reading situations in their full context rather than their surface presentation. And above all, they had to have a proven record of judgment grounded in justice and accountability, not in loyalty, not in personal advantage, not in the preferences of whoever held the most power within and without the communities they represent. This is the contrast that must be named plainly. Somalia’s federal parliament today is filled through a process shaped by clan arithmetic, financial transactions, and political patronage. The tree was filled through a process shaped by proven wisdom, plural knowledge, and demonstrated integrity. The parliament claims to be the more modern institution. In the matter of qualification standards for those who hold power over others, it is the more degraded one. None of the argument in this piece is against education, international engagement, or community and diaspora participation. Somalia cannot and should not close itself off from the world. Somali diaspora communities carry extraordinary intellectual, financial, and civic resources, and their engagement with the country’s development is not only legitimate but necessary-lifeline. International partnerships, when structured honestly,without back-thought interests, can support rather than distort. The argument is for the condition that makes all of these things useful rather than extractive, and that condition is rootedness. Rootedness in this context means political legitimacy that originates from within Somali society, not from without. It means leaders whose formation, however international their education, has been tested against the lived realities of Somali communities, whose judgment has been shaped by proximity to ordinary suffering rather than distance from it. It means accountability structures that run toward the people rather than away from them. It means the vetting of candidates and officials against standards of integrity that include their conduct during the years of violence, their record of resource, stewardship, and their demonstrated commitment to the communities they claim to represent. It means that the question of who leads Somalia is answered by Somali people operating from an informed position, not choreographed into endorsing a field pre-selected by external interests and internal power brokers before any vote is cast. Locally grounded durable solutions are not a slogan. They are a method. They require that the people designing and implementing governance carry real accountability to the communities affected, not just to the donor program cycle. The leader who can be questioned under the tree, figuratively or literally, who must return to the community and answer for what was done in its name, is a fundamentally different figure from the leader whose political survival is managed in a hotel conference room in another country or in an office of another country’s ministry of foreign affairs. The cost and the call The cost of the missing layer is not abstract. It shows up in a child who cannot access a functioning clinic. In a farmer whose land dispute goes unresolved for decades. In a woman whose testimony carries no weight in any formal institution. In a young person who sees clearly that the system was not built for them and was never intended to answer to them. These are not governance statistics. They are the accumulated cost of transactions conducted over the heads of ordinary Somali people, in their names, without their consent. Somalia has enormous intellectual capacity, an extraordinary diaspora, communities that have maintained social cohesion through decades of state collapse, and a younger generation that is watching and forming judgements about what is possible. What that generation needs to see is that the question of who leads and on what basis is being taken seriously, not managed, not performed for international audiences, but genuinely reckoned with as the foundational question of the country’s future. Identifying the missing layer clearly is the first act of rebuilding it. That layer is not a technical fix, not a new framework, not another round of international consultations. It is a political culture that demands rootedness as the price and base of power, that insists on accountability as a condition of legitimacy, and that refuses to extend either to figures whose record disqualifies them regardless of how effectively they have been rebranded. It is a civic infrastructure capable of making that demand stick. The state exists to serve its people. Somalia deserves leadership that answers to Somalia. Not to Mogadishu’s political season, not to the preferences of a capital on another continent, but to the lived realities of Somali people across every region of this country. That kind of leadership does not arrive by accident. It is cultivated, demanded, and chosen/elected. The question of who has a problem, who has an issue, was once answered under a tree, by people whose accountability ran in one direction only: toward the community. Rebuilding that direction is not a return to the past. It is the precondition for any viable future. Ammuuri waqtigeeday falantaa. All matters, time is their executor. The demand for rooted, accountable leadership in Somalia is not idealism. It is the most practical political position available to a people who have waited long enough. Wilo Abdulle, Email : Wilo.abdulle@gmail.com —— Wilo is Somali writer and governance practitioner working at the intersection of policy, equality, inclusion, human rights, community accountability, and the politics of development in the Horn of Africa. Her work on governance, accountability, and development in Somalia is rooted in a single conviction: that Somalia’s solutions must be Somalia’s own. items.title: Beeraley ku nool Galgaduud oo wajahaya nolol xumo markii gubay beero ay ku tiirsanaayeen
items.description: (ERGO) – Cali Xasan Maalin mid ka mid ah xaasaskiisa iyo gabar uu dhalay oo sanad jir ah ayaa u geeriyooday bishii Maarso nafaqo-darro, markii uu u awoodi waayay cunno qoyskiisa oo 18 qof ka kooban tan iyo dhamaadkii sanadkii hore. Sidoo kale wuxuu kari waayay in uu xilli hore geeyo xarun caafimaad dhaqaale xumo darteed. Reerka ninkaan ayaa ka mid ah in konton qoys oo beeralay ahaa oo galay xaalad nolol xumo ah oo aad u liidata. Bishii labaad ayaa laga gubay beero ay ku lahaayeen deegaanada Dab-dheer iyo Wabarka oo hoos taga magaalada Dhuusamareeb ee gobolka Galgadaduud, kuwaas oo noloshoodu ku tiirsanayd. Arrintan ayaa timid kaddib markii odayaasha dhaqanka ee deegaannadan ay dawladda ka codsadeen in beeraha la gubo. Waxay u arkeen xalka is qabqabsi dhul oo marar badan soo laalabtay. Ninkaan ayaa sheegay in beertiisa oo labo hektar ah uu bishii Diseembar ee sanadkii hore ku abuuray Dallagyo isku jiray raashin iyo khudaar, kuwaas oo dhamaan bas-beelay. Xilliga la gubayay ayuu sheegay in ay iib gayn u diyaarsanaayeen dalagyada. Xaaladdaas ayaa keentay nolol xumo aysan abid mudan. “Waxaan ku tiirsanahay koonbo baris ah iyo koonbo sonkor ah oo ay xaaskayga reeraha dariska ah ka soo dawarsato. Xaalada adag ayaan ku suganahay. Oday 77 jir ah ayaan ahay. Illahey mooye meel kale wax kama sugayno. Wixii na caawin kara waa u bahanahay.” Cali ayaa sheegay in uu cabsi ka qabo in dad kale ay kaga geeriyoodaan nafaqo darrada. Wuxuu tilmaamayin in xilligaan ay weli ka sii darayso xaaladda qoysaskiisa. Labo carruurtiisa ugu yar ayuu sheegay in hadda ay jirran yihiin muddo labo todobaad ah uusanna gayn goob caafimaad si xaaladdooda loo baxnaaniyo. Ganacsato ay qaraabo yihiin oo uu horay uga dayntay $230 oo uu isbitaalka ku geeyay dadkii geeriyooday ayay xusay in ay mid kale u diideen. Xaaladdaas darteed wuxuu sheegay in hadda uu ka rajo dhigay in uu dawo la raadiyo. Wuxuu sheegay in deeganka aysan ka jirin wax xarun caafimaad ah. Meesha ugu soo sokeysa waa magaalada Dhusamareeb oo deeganka Wabarka oo uu jooga u jirta qiyaastii in ka badan 30 km. Wuxuu xusay in lagu tago $50. Xaaladaha kale ee haysta qoyskiisa waxaa ka mid ah biyo yari. Waxay ku tiirsan yihiin hal jirgaan oo ay ka helaan dadka dariska la ah, kaas oo aan ku filnayn reerkiisa badan. Booyado biyaha ka keena deeganka lowrkii oo fustaadii iibiya $2 ayuu xusay in uusan awoodin. Wuxuu hadda gocanaya inuusan dib u tacbi karin beertiisa. “Deeganka Wabarka beer igu taalay ayaa la iga gubay. Waxaa amarka lagu gubay bixiyay rag odayaal ah. codsanayaa in raggii beertayda gubay shareecadda islaamka iyo calaadda in la ii hor keeno.” Wuxuu xusay in uu filayay in tacabkiisa uu ka faa’iido $800 haddii uu goosan laha, balse rajadaas ayuu ku hungoobay. Ninkaan oo sidoo kale ahaa xoolodhaqato ayaa roob la’aanta soo laalabatay ku wayay 65 arri ah oo uu dhaqanayay. Dhamaan beeralaydan oo ka siman saamaynta ayaa sheegay in aysan dib u yagleeli karin beerahoodi. Dayib Cali Axmed wuxuu tilmaamay in saddexdii bil ee la soo dhaafay ay qoyskiisa oo 10 qof ah wajahayaan nolol xumo liidato. Beer saddex hiktar ah oo ay noloshoodu ku tiirsanayd ayuu xusay in ay noqotay meel banaan. Dallagyo iskugu jiray galey, digir, masago, qaro iyo sinsin oo uu beertiisa bishii Janaayo ku galiyay $350 ayuu xusay in aysan waxbo uga babaadin, taas oo nolol xumo u horsedday reerkiisa. “Wax ii kaydsamay malahan wixii dhaw waa la iga gubay. Waxaan noqday qof isaga oo xoola leh inta laga qaatay meel cidlo ah ku soo dhacay oo gacan maran.” Dayib ayaa sheegay in reerkiisu ay dabka ku shitaan raashin ay u soo dhiibaan dad ay ehel yihiin oo jooga magaalada Dhusamareeb, kuwaas oo uu u dan sheegtay. Dhanka kale qoyskiisa waxaa ku adag helida biyaha. Booyado 30 fuusta qaada ayaa deeganka Dab-dheer oo uu ku nool yahay ku keena $50, taas oo uusan awodin. Waxay ka soo dhaamiyaan magaalada Dhusamareeb oo u jirta qiyaastii in ka badan 20 km. Sido kale waxaa saamaynta ku sii kordhasay bac uu biyaha ku kaysdan jiray oo u dhex taallay beerta oo dabku qabsaday. Arrintaas ayaa ku qasabtay in uu mutaan baco ay leeyihiin reero daris la ah oo biyaha ku caawiya, kuwaas oo ay garabka uga soo qaataan Bishii saddexaad ayuu xusay in laga soo eryay iskuul hoose iyo dhexe oo ay dhiganayeen, markii uu awoodi waayay $25 oo wax lagu barayaay. Taclin la’aanta soo wajahday ayuu walwal ka muujiyay. “Waxyaaba badan oo ay beerta iga aadanayd ayaa banaanka ku soo dhacay. Marka wixii dhan waxay noqdeen wax aan gacan lagu hayn hadda iyo kow soo bilow.” Dayib ayaa sheegay in beerta uu markii hore ku billabay $1,500 oo uu qayb ka helay 50 ari ah oo uu iibsaday iyo qaar ay ku kabeen dad ay ehel yihiin. In hadda laga gubay oo uusana dib u aas-aasan karin ayuu xusay in ay walwal ku hayso. Dadka beeraha ka falanaya deegaanka oo aad u soo badanayay waayihii danbe ayaa keenay qilaaf soo noqnoqday oo sababay in la gubo dhamaan beeraha sida u sheegay Salaad Cali Cawaale oo ka mid odayaasha dhaqanka ee amarka bixiyay. Waxay saamaynta ugu xoogan gaartay dadkii hore beeraha u laha oo ay u ahaayeen halka il ee ay ku tiirsanayeen. Dhanka kale wuxuu sheegay in dadka deegaanka oo ah xoola dhaqato ay beeralayda caqabad ku noqdeen, maaddaama la wada xirmaystay dhulkii daaqsinka ahaa. Dhowr mar oo hore ayuu sheegay in ay isku dayeen in ay xal u helaan arrintaan, balse ay u tabar waayeen, taasi oo horsedday in ay doorteen in la gubo. “Muran iyo is qabqabsi bulshada oo qaarkood ay ka dhasheen xoolo la dhibaateeyay, islamarkaasna ku dhawaaday dagaal toos ah keenay ayaa sababay inaan amarka bixiyo, markii aan tashanay. Waana iska kaashanay maamulka iyo booliska Galmudug.” Dhanka kale taliska saldhiga Dhuusamareeb oo aan la xariirnay ayaa noo sheegen in arrintan ay ku fuliyeen codsi iyo saxiix uga yimid odayaasha dhaqanka ee deegaannadan. Beeraleyda soomaaliyeed oo u nugul isbeddelka cimilada oo saamayn soo laalabatay ku yeeshay ayaa dhanka kale la kulma caqabada aysan xamali karin oo curyaamiya wax soo saarkooda, nolol xumana u horseedda qoysaskooda. The post Beeraley ku nool Galgaduud oo wajahaya nolol xumo markii gubay beero ay ku tiirsanaayeen appeared first on Radio Ergo - Somali Humanitarian News and Information .

items.title: Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh: Waxaa Jira Dalal Shisheeye Oo Doonaya In Soomaaliya aysan weligeed hore u socon
items.description: Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, ayaa sheegay in ay jiraan dalal shisheeye oo aan dan ka lahayn horumarka Soomaaliya, kuwaas oo uu sheegay inay doonayaan in dalka uu ku sii jiro xaaladaha adag ee amni iyo horumar la’aanta. Madaxweynaha oo wareysi bixiyay ayaa sheegay in dowladda Federaalka ay si dhow ula socoto faragelinta dibadda iyo shaqsiyaadka gudaha dalka jooga ee uu ku eedeeyay inay u adeegayaan danaha shisheeye ee ka soo horjeeda horumarka Soomaaliya. Wareysiga ayuu Madaxweynaha kaga hadlay arrimo dhowr ah oo muhiim u ah dalka, kuwaas oo ay ka mid yihiin dhacdooyinkii ugu dambeeyay ee ka dhacay Soomaaliya, geeddi-socodka wax ka beddelka dastuurka, dagaalka ka dhanka ah Al-Shabaab, xiriirka dowladda Federaalka iyo dowlad-goboleedyada, faragelinta Israa’iil iyo arrimo kale. Si kastaba ha ahaatee Madaxweynuhu wuxuu sheegay in ay wadaan baaritaanno waaweyn oo ay ku wadaan dalalka shisheeye ee Soomaaliya hagar daamaynaya iyo shakhsiyaadka u adeegaya, islamarkaana ay dhowaan natiijaa soo bandhigi doonaan.

items.title: Ants Scandal, Political Turmoil, and Unpaid Troops: A Tumultuous Week Raises Serious Questions in Puntland
items.description: By Ahmed A. Yusuf Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni returned to Garowe recently after a two-week visit to the United Arab Emirates, but instead of providing answers about his trip, his arrival has triggered a cascade of questions surrounding political infighting, unpaid security forces, a bizarre ant-smuggling controversy, and the reported arrest of a man who gifted his horse to former Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. As has become increasingly common, President Deni offered no public briefing on the purpose of his frequent UAE visits, the meetings he held, or the outcomes of discussions conducted abroad. For many Puntland residents, the silence has become familiar. Over the past several years, the president has made numerous visits to the Gulf state, yet details of those trips have often remained largely undisclosed, fueling speculation and public curiosity. A Public Rebuke Sparks Internal Rift The controversy began almost immediately upon the president’s return. Sources close to the Puntland Presidency claim that President Deni publicly reprimanded State Minister of the Presidency Abdifitah Mohamed Abdinur shortly after arriving at Garowe Airport. According to individuals familiar with the incident, the criticism occurred in the presence of government officials and members of the public, reportedly leaving the minister deeply angered and humiliated. Within hours, reports emerged that Abdifitah had departed for Ethiopia amid what sources describe as a growing dispute between him and the president. Neither side has publicly commented on the reported disagreement, but the incident has fueled speculation about internal divisions at Puntland’s administration. The Ant Scandal Nobody Saw Coming If the reported political fallout was unexpected, the issue allegedly at its center has left many observers stunned. Multiple sources claim that tensions within the Puntland Presidency are linked to foreign nationals from the Philippines and China who were reportedly brought into Puntland and are allegedly connected to the illegal export of Ants. Yes, ants. The allegations involve the trafficking of rare ant species that can fetch significant prices in specialized international markets . While the claims remain unverified, the mere suggestion that an ant-export operation could become entangled in a political dispute inside Puntland’s highest office has captivated public attention. Somali Ants The episode has generated widespread discussion across social media and political circles, with many asking how a controversy involving insects evolved into a matter of state-level political conflict. Unpaid Security Forces Block Roads Meanwhile, President Deni’s return also coincided with growing unrest among Puntland’s security forces. Members of the Puntland Police Rapid Response Unit, who recently completed training at the Carmo Police Academy, reportedly blocked several key roads in Garowe while protesting unpaid salaries. Although authorities eventually persuaded the troops to reopen the roads, the demonstration highlighted longstanding frustrations among security personnel who say they have endured chronic delays in receiving their wages. Local sources claim that some officers have abandoned their posts altogether, while others have returned to their home communities after losing hope that salary arrears would be paid. The situation has raised uncomfortable questions, particularly because the units involved are among Puntland’s specially trained forces. Critics are asking why elite security personnel continue to face salary shortages despite years of international support for Puntland’s security sector. Civil servants have voiced similar complaints, with some government employees alleging that they receive only a few months of salary payments in a typical year. The Horse Gift That Became a Political Controversy Yet perhaps the most surprising story of all involves an elderly Puntland resident and a horse. Reports widely circulated on social media claim that authorities detained a man after he publicly announced that he had gifted one of his personal horses to former Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. The reported arrest has sparked bewilderment and debate. Critics argue that if the reports are accurate, the incident raises serious questions about individual freedoms and political tolerance. They note that the horse was reportedly private property belonging to the man himself, not state-owned property, and that no allegations of theft or criminal conduct have been publicly presented. The government has not publicly explained the circumstances surrounding the reported detention. The controversy has quickly become a symbol of the broader political polarization that increasingly characterizes relations between supporters of Puntland’s leadership and those aligned with political actors in Mogadishu. More Questions Than Answers Taken individually, each of these developments would be noteworthy. Together, they have produced one of the most unusual political weeks Puntland has witnessed in recent memory: an unexplained foreign trip, reports of a presidential dispute with a senior official, allegations involving international ant trafficking, protests by unpaid security forces, and a controversy surrounding a horse gifted to a former president. For many Puntland residents, the common thread running through these events is a growing demand for transparency. As speculation continues to mount, one question remains unanswered: are these isolated incidents occurring at the same time, or do they point to deeper political and administrative challenges emerging beneath the surface of Puntland’s government? Until officials provide clearer explanations, the mystery surrounding this extraordinary week is likely to continue. Ahmed A. items.title: Senegal Football Federation clarifies viral airport security check video in US
items.description: WASHINGTON -The Senegal Football Federation on Tuesday clarified the circumstances surrounding a viral social media video showing members of the Senegal national team undergoing security screening checks after arriving in the US for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The federation said in a statement that the footage has led to misunderstandings online, with some reports incorrectly suggesting that the security checks took place upon the team’s arrival in San Antonio, Texas. “Contrary to some reports, the security screening did not take place upon the team’s arrival in San Antonio. Rather, it was conducted during boarding at Raleigh airport on Sunday, June 7, 2026, before the flight’s departure,” the federation said in a statement. The federation said the delegation traveled directly from its hotel in Raleigh, North Carolina to the airport tarmac by bus as part of a special travel arrangement. Players and staff then completed all required security and police procedures at the aircraft itself, rather than passing through the airport terminal and public boarding areas, it added. “The arrangement was primarily intended to optimize the delegation’s travel time and facilitate boarding of the private flight to San Antonio. “We wish to emphasize that the procedure was carried out in full compliance with airport security regulations and that no unusual incidents were reported,” it said. The federation added that the private flight operated without any issues and that the entire delegation arrived safely in San Antonio. The clarification comes as Senegal continues its preparations in the US ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which begins this week across the US, Canada and Mexico. Source: AA The post Senegal Football Federation clarifies viral airport security check video in US appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: Ruto oo si adag uga hadlay soo celinta Cartan, kuna tilmaamay qalad laga galay…
items.description: Nairobi (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Kenya, William Ruto oo ka hadlay dhacdada garsooraha Soomaaliyeed ee caanka ah Cumar Cartan oo laga soo celiyay dalka Mareykanka ayaa si adag u dhaliilay dowladda Mareykanka oo ka hor istaagtay inuu garsoore ka noqdo koobka adduunka ee FIFA 2026. Cumar Cartan oo ku guuleystay abaal-marinta garsooraha ugu fiican qaaradda Afrika sanadkii 2025 ayaa laga celiyay garoonka caalamiga ah ee Miami kadib markii saraakiisha kastamka iyo ilaalinta xuduudaha Mareykanka (CBP) ay sheegeen inay jiraan walaacyo la xiriira baaritaannada amniga iyo hubinta xogtiisa. Cartan ayaa sitay baasaboorka diblomaasiga ah ee Soomaaliya, waxaana markaas dib loogu celiyay magaalada Ankara ee caasimadda dalka Turkiga. Madaxweyne William Ruto ayaa ku tilmaamay tallaabadaas mid aan cadaalad ahayn, isagoo sheegay inay dhaawacayso sumcadda iyo dadaalka ciyaartooyda iyo garsoorayaasha Afrika ee ka qeyb-gala tartamada caalamiga ah. “Tallaabada Mareykanka looga soo celiyay Garsoore Cumar Cartan waa qalad weyn oo laga galay Afrika,” ayuu yiri Madaxweynaha Kenya, William Ruto. Sidoo kale, hoggaamiyeyaal kale oo Afrikaan ah ayaa cambaareeyay go’aanka Mareykanka, iyagoo ku baaqay in si degdeg ah dib loogu eego arrinta si Cumar Cartan loogu oggolaado inuu ka qeyb-galo tartanka ugu weyn kubadda cagta adduunka. Dhacdadan ayaa dhalisay dood xooggan oo ka taagan qaaradda Afrika, iyadoo taageerayaal badan iyo mas’uuliyiin isboorti ay walaac ka muujiyeen saameynta ay arrintani ku yeelan karto ka qeybgalka Afrika ee munaasabadaha caalamiga ah. Si kastaba, Garsoore Cartan ayaa shalay ku soo laabta dalka, isagoo si weyn loogu soo dhaaeeyay magaalada Muqdisho. Cartan oo lagu waday in uu noqdo qofkii ugu horeeyay ee Soomaali ah oo garsoore ka noqda final-ka loobka adduunka ayaa Isniintii laga saaray liiska, kaddib markii laga diiday inuu gudaha u galo dalka Mareykanka. items.title: Tartanka Koobka Adduunka ee 2026 oo ka furmay Mexico City
items.description: Tartanka Koobka Kubadda Cagta Adduunka ee FIFA 2026 ayaa caawa caweyskii ka furmay dalkaasi Mexico, saacadda Geeska Afrika markay ahayd 10:00pm, kuna beegan 1:00pm waqtiga maxaliga ee Mexico. Tartankan ayaa ka furmay Garoonka Kubadda Cagta Estadio Azteca ee Caasimadda Mexico City, waxaana lagu daahfuray Xulalka Mexico iyo South Africa oo ku wada jira Group A. Koobka Adduunka ee FIFA oo afartii sannaba mar la qabto ayaa waxaa sanadkan wada martigelinaya dalalka Mexico, Mareykanka iyo Canada. Koobka Adduunka ee FIFA 2026 ayaa ah tartankii ugu weynaa ee taariikhda, waxaana ka qaybgelaya 48 xul oo loo qaybiyay 12 Group oo min afar ah. Dhacdadan ayaa waxay ka kooban tahay 104 ciyaarood oo 16 magaalo lagu qabanayo. Labada kooxood ee ugu sarreya Group walba iyo sideedda kooxood ee ugu fiican kaalinta 3aad ayaa u gudbaya wareegga 32-ka. Tartanka ayaa lagu wadaa in 19-ka bisha July lagu soo geba-gabeeyo Garoonka Kubadda Cagta MetLife ee dalkaasi Mareykanka, halkaas oo ciyaarta finalka ay ku ciyaari doonaan labada kooxood ee isugu soo hara tartankaasi.

items.title: Nearly 118 million people were displaced by conflict and persecution last year, UN says
items.description: The U.N. refugee agency said forced displacement of people due to conflict or persecution fell in 2025 for the first time in a decade. But the agency warned in its annual report Thursday that 118 million people who had to flee their homes or nations is still alarmingly high. A look at the agency’s Global Trends Report on refugees and displaced people, by the numbers: The total number of people forcibly displaced by conflict, violence or persecution at the end of 2025 was 117.8 million. The figure includes refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced and other groups in need of international protection. It’s the first time in a decade the statistic fell. Behind the decline is both an increase in people who returned home and the fact that many refugees acquired citizenship of their host countries, among other reasons, said Tarek Abou Chabake, the U.N. agency’s chief statistician. The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees warned the number of those displaced globally, mostly by conflict, was unacceptably high. 39% Percentage of children among 41.6 million refugees last year. While Colombia, Germany and Turkey hosted more than 2 million refugees each, the majority live in low- to middle-income countries. Despite a 3% fall from the previous year, 5.4 million people crossed an international border in 2025 seeking refuge. 7 out of 10 Seven out of 10 refugees have lived in exile for five years or more, often trapped in sprawling camps in poor nations. “Humanitarian assistance has saved lives,” High Commissioner for Refugees Barham Salih said, adding that “it was never intended to sustain generations of people indefinitely.” The agency aims to slash by half the number of refugees in protracted displacement who are dependent on humanitarian assistance by 2035. 69 million There were 68.7 million people displaced within their countries last year. The ongoing war in Sudan was behind the largest displacement in the world with 9.1 million people forced to flee their homes. Colombia, Syria, Yemen and Afghanistan also have large displaced populations. Projections for 2026 did not look much better. With the Iran war erupting in February, 3.2 million people had been displaced by March inside Iran, and by mid-May, 1 million were displaced inside Lebanon. “This is truly unacceptable and we must make sure this doesn’t become a new normal,” Salih said. Three countries — Syria, Afghanistan and Sudan — saw 90% of the 4.4 million refugee return home in 2025. The number was the second highest since UNHCR began keeping records six decades ago. Another 10.3 million internally displaced people returned to their areas of origin last year. But Salih warned that many of those who went back did so under pressure and without basic infrastructure and conditions for a dignified life. “Voluntary returns to post-conflict Syria and returns under pressure to Afghanistan are not the same thing,” Salih said. 4.5 million The number of stateless people, of which the Rohingya from Myanmar make up the largest group. The majority of the stateless people live in Bangladesh, Ivory Coast, Thailand and Myanmar. Only 46,000 acquired citizenship in 2025. 82,000 The number of refugees resettled, which fell sharply from 188,000 in 2024. That’s a fraction of those in need, Salih said, as he urged governments to expand legal pathways for refugees to be relocated. “Every dangerous sea crossing and every death in the desert represents a failure of the international community,” Salih said. “The human cost of the failure is measured not with statistics but with lives.” Source: AP The post Nearly 118 million people were displaced by conflict and persecution last year, UN says appeared first on WardheerNews .

But Salih warned that many of those who went back did so under pressure and without basic infrastructure and conditions for a dignified life. “Voluntary returns to post-conflict Syria and returns under pressure to Afghanistan are not the same thing,” Salih said. 4.5 million The number of stateless people, of which the Rohingya from Myanmar make up the largest group. The majority of the stateless people live in Bangladesh, Ivory Coast, Thailand and Myanmar. Only 46,000 acquired citizenship in 2025. 82,000 The number of refugees resettled, which fell sharply from 188,000 in 2024. That’s a fraction of those in need, Salih said, as he urged governments to expand legal pathways for refugees to be relocated. “Every dangerous sea crossing and every death in the desert represents a failure of the international community,” Salih said. “The human cost of the failure is measured not with statistics but with lives.” Source: AP The post Nearly 118 million people were displaced by conflict and persecution last year, UN says appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: Trump oo baajiyay duqeymihii IRAN – Maxaa isbeddelay?
items.description: Washington (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Mareykanka, Donald Trump ayaa ku dhawaaqay inuu baajiyay duqeymihii la qorsheeyay ee dalka Iran, isagoo tilmaamay suurtagalnimada in heshiis rasmi ah lala saxiixdo Tehran kadib wada-hadallo heer sare ah oo dhexmaray labada dhinac. “Iyadoo lagu saleynayo xaqiiqda ah in wada-hadallada lala leeyahay Jamhuuriyadda Islaamiga ah ee Iran la gaarsiiyay heerkii ugu sarreeyay ee hoggaanka Iran ayna ansixiyeen, waxaan… baajiyay duqeymihii iyo weerarradii qorsheysnaa ee caawa lagu qaadi lahaa Iran,” ayuu Trump ku qoray bartiisa bulshada ee Truth Social. Trump ayaa sheegay in “qodobadii ugu dambeeyay” ee heshiiska ay ansixiyeen dhammaan dhinacyada ku lugta leh, inkastoo uusan bixin faahfaahin dheeraad ah oo ku saabsan waxyaabaha rasmiga ah ee lagu heshiiyay. Wuxuu intaas ku daray in waqtiga iyo goobta saxiixa rasmiga ah dhowaan lagu dhawaaqi doono. Si kastaba, madaxweynaha Mareykanka ayaa xaqiijiyay in go’doominta dhinaca badda ee ciidamada badda Mareykanka ay ku hayaan dekedaha Iran, taas oo bilaabatay bartamihii bishii Abriil ay sii jiri doonto ilaa inta si buuxda looga dhammaystirayo heshiiskaas. Isbeddelka ku yimid hadalka Trump Farriintan dambe ayaa calaamad u ah isbeddel weyn oo ku yimid hannaankii hadalka Trump ee saacadihii hore ee Khamiista, markaas oo uu ku hanjabay duqeymo hor leh, isagoo sheegay in ciidamada Mareykanka ay dhowaan la wareegi doonaan kaabeyaasha dhaqaale ee ugu muhiimsan saliidda Iran. “Ciidamada Mareykanka waxay Iran ku garaaci doonaan si adag caawa,” ayuu Trump soo dhigay saacado ka hor. “Waqti aan fogeyn kadib, waxaan la wareegi doonaa Jasiiradda Kharg iyo xarumaha kale ee kaabeyaasha saliidda, waxaanan si buuxda u maamuli doonaa suuqyadooda saliidda iyo gaaska, si la mid ah sidii aan ku sameynay Venezuela.” Ahmiyadda istiraatiijiyadeed ee Jasiiradda Kharg Jasiiradda Kharg waxay udub-dhexaad u tahay dhoofinta saliidda dalka Iran. Weerar kasta oo lagu qaado kaabayaasheeda tamarta wuxuu cawaaqib-xumo weyn ku keeni karaa suuqyada saliidda adduunka oo markii horeba qarka u saarnaa burbur. Dhoofinta saliidda ayaa weli ah isha ugu muhiimsan ee dakhliga dowladda Iran, taas oo Jasiiradda Kharg ka dhigaysa hantida ugu muhiimsan ee dhinaca dhaqaalaha dalkaas. Khatarta dagaal loo dhan yahay oo dib u qarxa Go’aanka Trump ee barta bulshada ayaa imanaya kadib markii Mareykanka iyo Iran ay isweydaarsadeen weerarro culus maalintii saddexaad oo xiriir ah, taas oo Bariga Dhexe qarka u saartay dagaal ballaaran. Weerarkii u dambeeyay ee Mareykanka, oo socday ilaa subaxnimadii Khamiista ee waqtiga Iran, ayaa u muuqday mid ka xoog badan kuwii dhacay dhowrkii maalmood ee ka horreeyay. Iran ayaa soo saartay macluumaad aad u yar oo ku saabsan baaxadda khasaaraha gaaray, waxayna sheegtay inay gantaallo uga jawaabtay dhinaca waddamada Kuweyt, Baxrayn iyo Urdun, sidii ay samaysay maalintii ka horreysay. Ciidamada Mareykanka ayaa sii wada xannibaadda dhinaca badda, iyagoo sheegay in Khamiistii ay gantaal ku dhufteen markab taangi ah oo isku dayayay inuu qaado saliidda Iran si ay u curyaamiyaan. Mas’uul u dhashay dalka Hindiya ayaa sidoo kale xaqiijiyay in weerar uu Mareykanku ku qaaday markab ganacsi oo kale horraantii toddobaadkan uu ku dilay saddex badmaax oo u dhashay Hindiya. Isweydaarsigan cusub ee madaafiicda iyo gantaalaha ayaa yimid xilli dadaallada nabadeed ay u muuqdeen kuwo istaagay. Trump ayaa horay uga digay Tehran inay “bixin doonto qiimaha” haddii horumar laga gaari waayo wada-hadallada. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda ee Iran ayaa bayaan ay soo saartay ku sheegtay in weerarrada Mareykanka ay “si dhab ah uga dhigeen xabbad-joojinta mid aan macno lahayn,” inkastoo aysan si rasmi ah u sheegin inay ka baxday xabbad-joojinta. Loolanka marinka Hormuz iyo barnaamijka nukliyeerka Udub-dhexaadka wada-hadallada ayaa ah xayiraadda ay Iran saartay Marinka Hormuz, taas oo carqaladeysay saadka tamarta adduunka, kor u qaadday qiimaha shidaalka, kuna qaalisay cuntada iyo waxyaabaha aasaasiga ah ee caalamka oo dhan. Iran ayaa ku dhawaaqday in marinkaas la xiray, laakiin ma cadda waxa ay taasi ka dhigan tahay maadaama ay markii horeba si weyn u xaddidday isu-socodka biyahaas. Hoggaanka Dhexe ee Ciidamada Mareykanka (CENTCOM) ayaa diiday sheegashada Iran, Trump-na wuxuu sheegay in Mareykanku uu sameeyay hawlgal qarsoodi ah toddobaadyadii la soo dhaafay si maraakiibta looga dhex mariyo marinkaas xasaasiga ah. Dhinaca kale, labada dhinac ayaa weli isku khilaafsan barnaamijka nukliyeerka ee Iran. Tehran waxay ku adkeysaneysaa inuu yahay mid nabdoon, balse Mareykanka iyo Israa’iil ayaa ka cabsi qaba in loo isticmaalo dhisidda hub atomik ah, sababo la xiriira kaydka weyn ee yuraaniyamta la hodmiyay ee ay Iran haysato. Mareykanka iyo Israa’iil ayaa caddeeyay in sababta ugu weyn ee ay dagaalka u galeen 28-kii Febraayo ay ahayd sidii loo hubin lahaa in Iran aysan waligeed awood u yeelan karin inay soo saarto hubka nukliyeerka. items.title: Maamulka gobolka Banaadir oo go’aamiyay in waddooyinka Muqdisho…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Maamulka gobolka Banaadir ayaa soo saaray go’aan cusub oo lagu mamnuucayo in lo’da lagu sii daayo waddooyinka magaalada Muqdisho, si wax looga qabto dhibaatooyinka la xiriira nadaafadda iyo bilicda caasimadda. Afhayeenka Maamulka Gobolka Banaadir, Saalax Xasan Cumar (Saalax Dheere) ayaa warbaahinta la wadaagay go’aan kasoo baxay Guddoomiyaha Gobolka Banaadir ahna Duqa Muqdisho, Xasan Maxamed Xuseen (Muungaab), kaas oo mamnuucaya lo’da lagu daayo waddooyinka magaalada. Go’aankan ayaa la sheegay inuu yimid kadib wada-tashi uu guddoomiyuhu la yeeshay qoysaska lo’da ku dhaqda gudaha Muqdisho iyo sidoo kale cabashooyin muddo dheer ka jiray caasimadda oo la xiriiray saameynta ay lo’du ku leedahay isu socodka iyo nadaafadda magaalada. Maamulka gobolka ayaa sheegay in lo’da lagu sii daayo waddooyinka ay sababto wasakh iyo nadaafad-darro ka dhalata saxarada xoolaha, taas oo saameyn ku yeelata caafimaadka bulshada iyo deegaanka, isla markaana dhaawacda muuqaalka guud ee caasimadda. Sidoo kale, maamulka ayaa xusay in lo’du ay carqalad ku noqoto isu socodka gaadiidka, iyadoo mararka qaar sababta shilal, ciriiri iyo khataro saameeya badqabka dadka iyo gaadiidka isticmaala waddooyinka caasimadda. Dhanka kale, maamulka ayaa tilmaamay in lo’da lagu daayo goobaha dadweynaha ay caqabad ku tahay dadaallada lagu dhiraynayo laguna qurxinayo magaalada Muqdisho, maadaama ay baabi’iso geedaha iyo dhirta lagu beero waddooyinka iyo goobaha cagaaran. Waxaa sidoo kale la sheegay inay jirto khatar caafimaad oo ka dhalan karta caanaha iyo hilibka xoolaha quuta wasakhda iyo qashinka lagu tuuro goobaha furan. Guddoomiyaha gobolka Banaadir ayaa amray in si buuxda loo mamnuuco lo’da lagu sii daayo waddooyinka Muqdisho, iyadoo dadka dhaqda lo’da la siiyey muddo laba toddobaad ah oo ka bilaabanaysa 16-ka Juun 2026 kuna eg 27-ka Juun 2026, si ay u xareeyaan xoolahooda. Maamulka ayaa sheegay in tallaabooyin sharci ah laga qaadi doono cid kasta oo lagu arko lo’ ay waddooyinka ku sii daysay marka ay dhammaato muddada loo qabtay, isagoo ugu dambayn uga mahadceliyey shacabka iyo qoysaska dhaqda lo’da wada-shaqaynta ay muujiyeen. items.title: Opposition Unity Tested as Farmaajo Dispute Exposes Deepening Fault Lines Ahead of Halane Talks
items.description: By Mohamed A Yasin At a moment when Somalia’s opposition is under increasing pressure to present a united front against the federal government, a new political dispute threatens to undermine months of efforts aimed at building a broad coalition capable of influencing the country’s future direction. Reports emerging from political circles in Mogadishu indicate that serious disagreements have surfaced within the Future Council, one of the country’s most prominent opposition platforms, over the proposed participation of former President Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo in an upcoming government-opposition dialogue expected to take place in Halane under the facilitation of Turkish diplomats. The disagreement may appear procedural on the surface, centering on the number of delegates each political bloc should send to the talks. In reality, however, it reflects a much deeper struggle over influence, leadership, and the future structure of Somalia’s opposition movement. Although the opposition coalition includes a diverse range of political figures, including many who served in senior positions under former Presidents Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo and Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, disagreements have reportedly emerged over representation in the ongoing negotiations.  According to sources familiar with the negotiations, some members of the Future Council have objected to Farmaajo’s political camp being granted representation equal to that of the opposition coalition itself. The issue has reportedly become one of the most contentious subjects in preparations for the talks, raising concerns that internal rivalries could overshadow the larger political challenges facing the country. The dispute comes at a time when many Somalis are increasingly demanding greater unity among opposition groups. Critics argue that while the federal government remains organized around a clear political agenda, opposition figures continue to spend valuable time debating personalities, positions, and political status rather than focusing on common objectives. The controversy has exposed a recurring problem within Somali opposition politics: the tendency for individual ambitions and factional interests to take precedence over collective strategy. Former Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire and MP Abdirahman Abdishakur are reported to be among those who have questioned the proposal to grant Farmaajo’s camp representation equal to that of the Future Council. Supporters of this position argue that the coalition has spent months organizing meetings, coordinating political positions, and engaging in consultations, while Farmaajo’s political network has only recently become involved in the process. Those close to this camp maintain that representation should reflect political participation and organizational investment rather than simply the prominence of individual political figures. However, opponents of that argument see the matter differently. They argue that no opposition alliance can credibly claim to represent Somalia’s entire political opposition while simultaneously attempting to limit the participation of one of the country’s most recognizable political figures. Whether one supports or opposes Farmaajo politically, they argue, his influence within Somali politics remains undeniable. More importantly, they warn that excluding or marginalizing major political actors would send the wrong signal at a time when opposition unity is being tested by increasingly complex political developments. The controversy has also reignited debate about who has the authority to determine the composition of Somalia’s opposition movement. The exclusionary approach argue that no individual politician or faction possesses a monopoly over opposition politics. They contend that the opposition should be broad enough to accommodate differing viewpoints and political traditions while remaining focused on shared concerns regarding governance, constitutional issues, elections, and national reconciliation. For many analysts, the issue is not merely whether Farmaajo attends the talks. The larger question is whether Somalia’s opposition can develop a culture of political cooperation that transcends personal rivalries and historical disagreements. The challenge is particularly significant because opposition alliances in Somalia have often struggled to maintain cohesion once questions of leadership and representation emerge. Former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed has reportedly adopted a more conciliatory position. Widely regarded as one of the most experienced political figures in the country, Sharif is said to favor a broader and more inclusive opposition platform that accommodates all major stakeholders. His approach reflects a belief shared by many political observers that effective opposition politics requires coalition-building rather than gatekeeping. Indeed, several analysts point out that opposition movements become strongest when they expand their political base rather than narrow it. Attempts to determine who qualifies as a “legitimate” opposition figure often create new divisions that ultimately benefit the incumbent government. This reality has not gone unnoticed among political commentators. A growing number of analysts argue that the debate over Farmaajo’s participation risks distracting attention from the substantive issues that originally brought opposition groups together. These include concerns about constitutional disputes, electoral frameworks, political inclusion, federal-state relations, and the concentration of power within federal institutions. Instead of focusing on these national questions, critics say opposition leaders increasingly appear preoccupied with internal disputes that ordinary citizens view as secondary to the country’s broader challenges. Diplomats involved in the process are said to view opposition unity as a critical prerequisite for meaningful political dialogue. items.title: Cumar Cartan oo lagu dhawaaqay inuu dhex-dhexaadin doono finalka Super Cup-ka Yurub
items.description: Nairobi (Caasimada Online) – Kadib markii loo sheegay Garsoore Cumar Cartan inuusan wax garsoor ah ka qaban doonin Koobka Adduunka, iyadoo dib looga soo celiyay dalka Mareykanka ayaa waxaa lagu abaal mariyay inuu qaban doona tartan weyn. Xiriirka ciyaaraha Yurub ee UEFA ayaa ku dhawaaqday in garsooraha u dhashay dalka Soomaaliya ee Cumar Cartan uu dhex-dhexaadin doonaa ciyaarta weyn ee Super Cup-ka ee dhexmari doonta kooxaha Paris Saint-Germain iyo Aston Villa. Cartan ayaa loo doortay inuu noqdo mid ka mid ah garsoorayaasha matalaya qaaradda Afrika ee Koobka Adduunka, baddalkeedase waxaa diiday hay’adda Ilaalada Xuduudaha iyo Kastamka Mareykanka (CBP) ee Garoonka Caalamiga ah ee Miami, waxaana dib loogu soo celiyay duulimaad dalka Turkiga. Cartan ayaa ku adkaystay inuu watay waraaqihii saxda ahaa iyo dhalashadii/viisadii saxda ahayd, laakiin maamulka Trump ayaa u ogolaan waayay inuu galo gudaha Mareykanka. Go’aankan ayaa dhaliyay carro xooggan oo ka timid adduunka kubadda cagta, kuwaas oo garab istaagay garsooraha Soomaaliyeed. UEFA ayaa muujisay garab istaaggeeda iyadoo u dhiibtay hoggaaminta ciyaar weyn oo dhici doonta bilowga xilli ciyaareedka soo socda. Kadib markii ay dib u soo celiyeen saraakiisha xadka Mareykanka, guddiga maamula kubadda cagta Yurub ayaa xaqiijiyay inuu garsoori doono kulanka Super Cup-ka ee bisha Ogosto ka dhici doona magaalada Salzburg. “Go’aanka Artan loogu magacaabay inuu garsoore ka noqdo ciyaarta Koobka Super Cup-ka ee UEFA ayaa loo qaatay iyadoo la raacayo hannaanka Is-fahamka ee dhowaan ay kala saxiixdeen UEFA iyo CAF si loo dhiiri-geliyo iskaashiga dhinacyo badan, oo ay ku jirto garsooridda. “UEFA iyo CAF waxaa ka go’an ballanqaad wadajir ah oo ku aaddan horumarinta kubbadda cagta ee heer kasta iyo horumarinta qiyaamka asaasiga ah ee midnimada, sinnaanta, iyo takoor-la’aanta,” ayaa lagu yiri qoraal kasoo baxay UEAFA. Madaxweynaha UEFA, Alexander Ceferin ayaa sidoo kale ku daray in Cumar Cartan uu yahay garsoore daddaalaya, dhallinyaro ah oo aad u wanaagsan laakiin haddana khibrad leh, kaasoo isku caddeeyay heerka tartanka ugu sarreeya ee Xiriirka Kubbadda Cagta Afrika. “Kubbadda cagta waxaa loo sameeyay inay dadka isku xirto, UEFA-na waxay rabtaa inay muujiso ixtiraamka ay u heyso Cumar iyo xirfaddiisa garsoornimo ee aadka u sarreysa, taasoo u horseeday magacaabistan sharafta leh. Waxaan u mahadcelinayaa saaxiibkay, Madaxweynaha CAF Patrice Motsepe, oo si xamaasad leh u taageeray dadaalkayaga.” Cartan waxaa si weyn loogu aqoonsan yahay mid ka mid ah garsoorayaasha ugu fiican Afrika, wuxuuna qarka u saarnaa inuu noqdo wakiilkii ugu horreeyay ee abid dalkiisa uga qeyb gala Koobka Adduunka. Waxaa loo magacaabay sarkaalka ugu fiican qaaradda, isagoo sidoo kale soo maamulay labo ciyaarood oo ka tirsan Koobka Qaramada Afrika. Tallaabadaan ayaa durba qoyska ciyaaraha ee dunida ku kala firirsan aad u soo dhoweeyay, iyagoo taageero xad-dhaaf ah u muujiyay garsooraha Soomaaliyeed, taasoo uu ku hilmaamay hab-dhaqanka xun ee saraakiisha socdaalka Mareykanka ula dhaqmeen Cumar Camar. The post Cumar Cartan oo lagu dhawaaqay inuu dhex-dhexaadin doono finalka Super Cup-ka Yurub appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh oo booqasho ku tegay Magaalada Jowhar (SAWIRRO)
items.description: Madaxweynaha Somaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa maanta gaaray Magaalada Jowhar ee Xarunta Dowlad Goboleedka Hirshabelle. Madaxweynaha oo ka ambabaxay Magaalada Muqdisho ayaa waxaa Garoonka Diyaaradaha Maxamed Dheere ku soo dhaweeyay masuuliyiin uu ugu sarreyo Madaxweynaha Hirshabelle, Cali Cabdullaahi Xuseen (Cali Guudlaawe). Safarka Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda ayaa la xiriira, sidii uu xarigga uga jari lahaa mashaariic horumarineed oo laga hirgeliyay Xarunta Dowlad Goboleedka Hirshabelle ee Jowhar. “Madaxweynaha Dowladda Somaliya, Dr. Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud oo uu wehliyo Madaxweyne Mudane Cali Cabdullaahi Xuseen (Cali Guudlaawe) ayaa si wadajir xarigga uga jaray saddex waddo oo kala ah 1. Horseed, 2. Hanti-wadaag iyo Jowhar-bile, kuwaas oo sahli doono isku socodka shacabka Caasimadda Hirshabelle.” Ayaa lagu yiri war ka soo baxay Madaxtooyada Hirshabelle. Socdaalkan ayaa noqonaya kiisii ugu horreyay ee Madaxweynaha Dowladda Federaalka uu sanadkan ku tago Hirshabelle, iyadoo deegaanada Hirshabelle haatan looga diyaargaroobayo doorashada soo socota.
